title: Rigveda 5.50: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.50: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.50 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 367v-368r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.50.1-3 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 4); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 367v
translation.original_text:
1viśvo̍ de̱vasya̍ ne̱tur marto̍ vurīta sa̱khyam | viśvo̍ rā̱ya i̍ṣudhyati dyu̱mnaṁ vṛ̍ṇīta pu̱ṣyase̍ ||
2te te̍ deva neta̱r ye ce̱mām̐ a̍nu̱śase̍ | te rā̱yā te hy ā̱3̱̍pṛce̱ sace̍mahi saca̱thyai̍ḥ ||
3ato̍ na̱ ā nṝn ati̍thī̱n ata̱ḥ patnī̍r daśasyata | ā̱re viśva̍m pathe̱ṣṭhāṁ dvi̱ṣo yu̍yotu̱ yūyu̍viḥ ||
translation.text:
1LET every mortal man elect the friendship of the guiding God. Each one solicits him for wealth and seeks renown to prosper him.
2These, leading God, are thine, and these here ready to speak after us. As such may we attain to wealth and wait with services on thee.
3So further honour as our guests the Hero Gods and then the Dames. May he remove and keep afar our foes and all who block our path.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 367v (numbered 40v by the scribe) (OPenn image 368, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.49.4 ‹-vāja-ratnāḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 368r (numbered 41r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.50.4 ‹-arṇāḥ dhīrāiva sanitā›. Verses 5.50.1-3 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1viśvaḥ | devasya | netuḥ | martaḥ | vurīta | sakhyam | viśvaḥ | rāye | iṣudhyati | dyumnam | vṛṇīta | puṣyase
2te | te | deva | netaḥ | ye | ca | imān | anu-śase | te | rāyā | te | hi | āpṛce | sacemahi | sacathyaiḥ
3ataḥ | naḥ | ā | nṝn | atithīn | ataḥ | patnīḥ | daśasyata | āre | viśvam | pathe--sthām | dviṣaḥ | yuyotuyūyuviḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 5.50.4-5 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 4); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 368r
translation.original_text:
4yatra̱ vahni̍r a̱bhihi̍to du̱drava̱d droṇya̍ḥ pa̱śuḥ | nṛ̱maṇā̍ vī̱rapa̱styo 'rṇā̱ dhīre̍va̱ sani̍tā ||
5e̱ṣa te̍ deva netā̱ ratha̱spati̱ḥ śaṁ ra̱yiḥ | śaṁ rā̱ye śaṁ sva̱staya̍ iṣa̱ḥstuto̍ manāmahe deva̱stuto̍ manāmahe ||
translation.text:
4Where fire is set, and swiftly runs the victim dwelling in the trough, He wins, with heroes in his home, friendly to man, like constant streams.
5May these thy riches, Leader God! that rule the car, be blest to us, Yea, blest to us for wealth and weal. This will we ponder praising strength, this ponder as we praise the God.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 368r (numbered 41r by the scribe) (OPenn image 368, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.50.4 ‹-arṇāḥ dhīrāiva sanitā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 368v (numbered 41v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.51.5 ‹-sutasya andhasaḥ abhi prayaḥ›. Verses 5.50.4-5 end on this page; 5.50.4 begins on fol. 367v (numbered 40v by the scribe).

4yatra | vahniḥ | abhi-hitaḥ | dudravat | droṇyaḥ | paśuḥ | nṛ-manāḥ | vīra-pastyaḥ | arṇāḥ | dhīrāiva | sanitā
5eṣaḥ | te | deva | netariti | rathaḥpatiḥ | śam | rayiḥ | śam | rāye | śam | svastaye | iṣaḥ-stutaḥ | manāmahe | deva-stutaḥ | manāmahe
